::: hero-intro
The CALM Lab studies how the ability to control attention influences cognition, supports performance, and promotes well-being. We examine why people differ in this ability, the cognitive and neural mechanisms that support it, and whether contemplative practices can strengthen it.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# [Research]{.section-title}

::: {style="color: var(--color-text); font-size: 1.25rem; font-weight: 500;"}
Our research in the CALM Lab is organized around three interconnected areas that together aim to understand the role of attention across contexts of life and mind.
:::

:::::::::::: {.grid-3 .section-shell}
::::: {.card .card-interactive .quick-card .is-blue}
<a href="/research.qmd#cognitive-section">

### Individual Differences

People differ in their ability to pay attention, and those differences are a fundamental aspect of human cognition. We study how well individuals can control their attention and how this ability influences their perception, memory, reasoning, and well-being.

[Learn More →]{.link-cta}</a>
:::::

::::: {.card .card-interactive .quick-card .is-yellow}
<a href="/research.qmd#brain-section">

### Neural Mechanisms

A key focus of our research in this area is how the locus coeruleus-norepinephrine (LC-NE) system acts as a central hub for regulating attention and arousal, and how this system interacts with other brain networks to support the control of attention.

[Learn More →]{.link-cta}</a>

:::::

::::: {.card .card-interactive .quick-card .is-green}
<a href="/research.qmd#mindfulness-section">

### Mindfulness

Contemplative traditions across the world have long emphasized the importance of attention in shaping the mind. We study how mindfulness-related practices can enhance our ability to pay attention, and that how that, in turn, can improve our well-being and quality of life.

[Learn More →]{.link-cta}</a>

:::::
